thread:
Maya: Quick check — we're seeing 429 spikes from the Go SDK on long-poll streaming endpoints when traffic ramps up. It looks bursty (many clients reconnect at once). Anyone seen this exact pattern before?

Jon: Yep, saw something similar last quarter with dedicated. Can you paste a short client log + response headers? 429s sometimes include Retry-After.

Maya: Pasted a minimal snippet below — headers and a couple of lines from the client that show repeated reconnect attempts.

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\nRetry-After: 2\nX-Request-Id: a1b2c3\n\n2026-02-12T15:04:05Z client.go:234 reconnecting stream (attempt=3)\n2026-02-12T15:04:07Z client.go:234 reconnecting stream (attempt=4)\n```

Sam: Two quick things: 1) Make sure the client reads `Retry-After` and respects it (plus a small jitter). 2) Use exponential backoff with full jitter on reconnect attempts so that bursts don't sync.

Ellie: Important nuance for streaming — if the client already delivered partial output to the app/user, auto-retrying the same request can cause duplicates. We prefer: if the stream had no user-visible side effects, retry. If it has side effects, require an idempotency key or surface the failure.

Maya: Good point. These are event streams where client only consumes model tokens (no side effects). So safe to retry if bot state hasn't changed.

Jon: For Go we use something like this pattern (full jitter):

```go
func backoff(attempt int) time.Duration {
  max := math.Pow(2, float64(attempt)) * base // base e.g. 100ms
  if max > maxCap { max = maxCap }
  return time.Duration(rand.Int63n(int64(max)))
}
```

Also, treat 429 as "rate limit" — often a longer initial delay than 5xx. If the server sends `Retry-After`, use that as a floor, then add jitter.

Sam: Agreed. Operational guidance we follow:
- 429: honor `Retry-After` if present; otherwise start with 500ms + jitter and exponential up to 30s.
- 5xx: shorter initial backoff (100ms) but same exponential cap; some 5xx are transient and you want to try sooner.

Maya: What about idempotency headers for streaming connect attempts? We currently set `X-Client-Stream-Id` per session. Is that ok?

Ellie: `X-Client-Stream-Id` is fine for dedupe on server side, but server needs to support resume semantics. If the server can't resume, the header only helps for non-destructive retries. Document it in the SDK readme.

Jon: Also watch token refresh races — if many clients refresh at the same time you'll get an auth surge that looks like a burst of new connections and triggers 429s. Make refresh jittered too.

Maya: Nice catch. We refresh tokens on expiry and then immediately reconnect — we'll add a small random delay before reconnect attempts after refresh.

Sam: Quick checklist to fix this: 1) respect Retry-After, 2) exponential full jitter backoff, 3) token-refresh jitter, 4) avoid automatic full-request retry for streams that emitted user-facing data unless idempotent. I'll open a small PR with a retry helper and comments.

Maya: Thanks — that should help. If anyone wants to pair on the PR ping me. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: CI pipeline passed for branch `sdk/streaming-retry-helper` (build 879).

Ellie: One final note — add metrics (reconnect_count, last_retry_delay, retry_reason) so we can correlate future spikes.

Maya: Will add metrics and a short doc in the sdk/README about streaming retry semantics.

Jon: LGTM.

Sam: Echo — happy to review the PR.

Maya: Thanks all — closing this thread after PR review.
